Posterior of the linear predictor

Source: R/posterior_predict.R
posterior_linpred.Rd

The posterior of the linear predictor eta at the training data with every component the fit estimated: fixed effects, the offset, formula random effects, spatial and temporal fields and latent() blocks. It is the quantity posterior_predict() pushes through the family, read here on the link scale; fitted.tulpa_fit() is its posterior mean at the training data and predict.tulpa_fit() summarizes it at new data.

On a nested-Laplace fit the posterior of each eta_i is the grid mixture sum_k w_k N(fitted_eta[k, i], fitted_eta_var[k, i]), and summary = TRUE reports its exact mean, SD and quantiles. A fit run with control$fitted_var = FALSE carries no within-cell variance, and its summary reports the mixture mean alone (source = "mode", sd and bounds NA). Every other fit summarizes its draws.

At newdata, a latent field is drawn at the new rows from its conditional distribution given the fitted field (within each hyperparameter cell and mixed over the cells, or given each stored draw of a sampler): a continuous field at the new locations, an areal or temporal field at the row's fitted unit or time (see predict.tulpa_fit()); these are the draws predict.tulpa_fit() summarizes, so the two agree to Monte Carlo error.

Usage

posterior_linpred(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tulpa_fit'
posterior_linpred(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  summary = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  seed = NULL,
  re_form = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A tulpa_fit object.

...

Passed to methods.

newdata

Optional data frame of covariates, read as in posterior_predict(). NULL (default) reads the training data.

ndraws

Number of draws (summary = FALSE, or a draw-based summary).

summary

Logical; return a per-observation summary instead of draws.

probs

The two probabilities of the reported interval.

seed

Optional integer seed (RNG state is restored on exit).

re_form

Which formula random-effect terms to condition on, as in posterior_predict().

Value

With summary = FALSE, an ndraws x n_obs matrix of draws. With summary = TRUE, a data frame with one row per observation: estimate, sd, conf.low, conf.high (at probs) and source ("mixture" for the exact grid mixture, "mode" for its mean alone, "sampled" for a draw summary).

See also

posterior_predict(), predict.tulpa_fit().

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(y = rpois(100, 4), x = rnorm(100), g = gl(10, 10))
fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "poisson", mode = "laplace")
#> Warning: tulpa(): `sigma_re` not supplied; conditioning on sigma_re = 1 for each of the 1 RE term(s). Pass `sigma_re` to override.
head(posterior_linpred(fit, summary = TRUE))
#>   estimate        sd conf.low conf.high  source
#> 1 1.487996 0.1528009 1.182013  1.791083 sampled
#> 2 1.449005 0.1550125 1.141495  1.750855 sampled
#> 3 1.485797 0.1523092 1.181792  1.792162 sampled
#> 4 1.429036 0.1646791 1.103815  1.748674 sampled
#> 5 1.527944 0.1731871 1.190870  1.857790 sampled
#> 6 1.549073 0.1910855 1.160851  1.921701 sampled
# }
